answer: Each agent must periodically solve a fresh cipher puzzle tied to its own identity and publish the proof on a public ledger, building a verifiable work history over time. Trust then flows like a river: steady, cumulative, and hard to fake. A newcomer starts alone on a bare knoll with zero history, and a sybil attacker who splits into many identities restarts from zero every time, so copying an identity buys no reputation and forging a long history costs more than any reward it could earn.
